text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Latvia and Sweden have signed an agreement on the readmission of illegal immigrants, seen as a step to introducing a visa-free regime.
- Latvia and Lithuania resume today talks on delimitation of their maritime border. They have no powers to discuss the possible sharing of potential oil fields in the Baltic Sea.

- Lithuanian parliament speaker Vytautas Landsbergis said he was told by oil firm Amoco that the company might break its oil exploration agreement with Latvia unless the sea border dispute between Latvia and Lithuania was settled soon.
- President Ulmanis said after meeting leaders of Fatherland & Freedom that Economy Minister Guntar Krasts should keep working in the government.
- Lattelekom said its 1996 net profit was 4.1 million lats.
- The Immigration board is to issue the first 10-15 so-called aliens passports to Latvia's non-citizens, mainly ethnic Russian speakers.
- About 15 tonnes of oil were washed ashore in Kurzeme, on the western coast of Latvia. Experts believe the oil has spilt from a tanker.

- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs said after meeting Russian first deputy foreign minister Igor Ivanov that Russian Foreign Minister Yevgueny Primakov will visit Latvia to attend the sixth session of the Baltic Sea Council on July 2-3.
- Krasts met representatives of two German companies, Lahmeyer International and Rogge Marine Consulting, to discuss the possibility of investing 100 million marks in the port of Liepaja.

- Ventspils Nafta and Lukoil may sign an agreement on guaranteed trans-shipment of at least two million tonnes of oil and oil products by Lukoil every year. In return, the company wants to be granted a 10-percent rebate in tariffs.
- The co-operation council of the governing factions has agreed to form a working group to revise pensions laws.
- The central depositaries of Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia may sign an agreement on forming a unified securities accounting system by the end of this year.
